title: Context of Scripture
definition: The context of Scripture is the surrounding passage, book, covenant setting, genre, and biblical storyline that helps readers understand a text rightly.
summary: Scripture should be read in context so God's meaning is not distorted.
christFocus: Jesus showed how individual passages fit within the larger redemptive storyline fulfilled in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Context protects the meaning of Scripture. Words, verses, and passages belong within chapters, books, covenants, and the whole Bible. Removing them from that setting can create confusion.

Context includes the immediate passage, the author's purpose, historical setting, literary form, and the wider story of redemption. It helps the reader hear what God has actually said.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many popular errors come from isolated verses detached from context. This doctrine matters because context helps protect believers from false promises, false guilt, and false teaching.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read before and after a verse. Ask how the passage fits the book and how the book fits the Bible's message. Refuse to use verses as slogans without understanding their setting.
